race.name: The Gravel of Marathon
race.tagline: Greece's first UCI gravel qualifier: three laps of a 31 km Lake Marathon loop on roughly 75 percent dirt.

vitals.start_format: UCI Gravel World Series age-category competition; exact wave schedule not published
vitals.registration: Registration is open through the organizer-linked ENDU platform for both official distances.
vitals.entry_fee: Not stated on the cited public organizer page
route_options: Long: 96 km / 59.7 mi with 1,320 m / 4,331 ft, roughly 75% off-road — qualifier for elites, men 19-59, and women 19-49
Short: 65 km / 40.4 mi with 1,150 m / 3,773 ft, roughly 75% off-road — qualifier for men 60+ and women 50+

climate.description: Mid-November in Attica is generally cooler than summer, but rain can turn the soft lake-edge dirt and farm roads into a different course. The race-specific forecast remains the authority close to the event.
challenges: Limited daylight late in the season

terrain.primary: Rocky climbs, rural dirt roads and repeated lakeside loops
terrain.surface: The UCI course page puts both routes at roughly 75% off-road: rocky climbing, rural dirt alternating with asphalt, four kilometres of soft dirt beside Lake Marathon, two shallow stream crossings, and five kilometres of asphalt through Grammatiko on the way out.
features: A 2 km rocky climb at 6% average, 9% maximum
A 500 m climb after the first stream
Four kilometres of soft dirt beside Lake Marathon
Three laps of the 31 km loop on the long course

gravel_god_rating.score_note: The inaugural Greek UCI qualifier published a clear course: a 31 km loop ridden three times, roughly 75 percent off-road, with short steep climbs. The unproven first-edition field and operations record hold it in Tier 3.

logistics.explanation: Marathon is roughly 40 km from Athens with broad local lodging choices, which is much easier than most destination gravel races. Airport transfer, city traffic, and bike transport still require planning, but the event is not remote.

length.explanation: The long course is 96 km, or 59.7 miles, inside the published score-two band. Three laps of the same 31 km loop make it a pacing problem because every steep feature returns.

technicality.explanation: The official course mixes a rocky opening climb, rural dirt and asphalt, soft lakeside dirt and two shallow stream crossings. It asks for mixed-surface control without claiming extreme singletrack.

elevation.explanation: The long course carries 1,320 metres, about 4,331 feet, of climbing, inside the published 4,000-6,000-foot band for score three. Most of it comes in short climbs repeated on each lap.

climate.explanation: November reduces the heat risk around Attica, while rain could materially change a course that is roughly 75 percent off-road. Conditions deserve equipment flexibility but are not inherently an extreme-climate challenge.

altitude.explanation: The Marathon and Lake Marathon course stays at low elevation. The 9-percent and 12-percent ramps hurt because they repeat, not because oxygen is scarce.

adventure.explanation: The race joins Lake Marathon, rural dirt roads, stream crossings and the town associated with the Battle of Marathon. Repeating terrain usually reduces adventure, but this loop has unusually strong place identity.

prestige.explanation: This is Greece's first UCI Gravel World Series race and a qualifier for the 2027 Worlds. That matters immediately, but an inaugural event has no race history or established status of its own.

race_quality.explanation: Bicycle Friendly Greece and the MBike team bring cycling-media and Athens Bike Festival experience, while the official course package is unusually specific. Actual race-day execution remains unproven until November.

experience.explanation: Starting at Marathon Stadium, racing beside the lake, crossing streams, and finishing in the centre of Marathon gives each lap a real narrative. The history-rich setting is memorable without relying on invented crowd claims.

community.explanation: The organizer has supported Greek cycling media since 1999 and the Athens Bike Festival since 2010. The specific gravel race is brand new, so established-organizer reach should not be confused with a mature race community.

field_depth.explanation: UCI qualification should draw strong Greek and regional age-group racers, but no start list or field size is published. The series status supports a competitive score, not a claim of elite international depth.

value.explanation: A 96 km UCI qualifier, roughly 75 percent off-road, with an official course description is a substantial product. With no public entry price in the cited page, the honest score is neutral rather than promotional.

expenses.explanation: Athens is internationally accessible and Marathon has varied lodging, but flights, bike transport, and multiple nights make this a high-cost trip for non-European athletes. Regional riders will spend much less.

course_description.character: A three-lap long course from Marathon Stadium. Riders cross town, climb 2 km on rocky terrain, pass Grammatiko on five kilometres of asphalt, cross a shallow stream and climb 500 m to reach a 31 km loop: rural dirt and asphalt, four kilometres of soft dirt beside Lake Marathon, a second stream, a 200 m soft-dirt climb at up to 12%, and six kilometres of dirt back to the loop start. The return retraces the way out to a finish in the centre of Marathon.
course_description.signature_challenge: Treating the first lap as reconnaissance, the second as work, and the third as a race, because the 12-percent climb and the streams come back every lap.

suffering_zones.label: Rocky opening climb
suffering_zones.desc: Soon after crossing town, a 2 km climb on rocky terrain averages 6 percent with a 9-percent maximum.

suffering_zones.label: Lake Marathon
suffering_zones.desc: Four kilometres of soft dirt beside the lake, entered at the second feed station.

suffering_zones.label: Greenhouse wall
suffering_zones.desc: After the greenhouses and a second shallow stream, a 200 m soft-dirt climb reaches 12 percent, then six kilometres of dirt close the loop.

biased_opinion.summary: Three laps sound less adventurous until you inspect the lap: rural dirt, lake-edge dirt, two streams and a 12-percent soft-dirt ramp. The repeat format makes pacing brutally legible. If lap one feels heroic, lap three will collect the debt.
strengths: Easy access from Athens relative to most gravel destinations
weaknesses: Current public page omits aid and cutoff details
biased_opinion.bottom_line: One of the strongest new-race intakes in the catalog because the organizer published the actual demands. Tier 3 today; the first edition will decide whether it deserves more.

logistics.airport: Athens International Airport (ATH), with Marathon approximately 40 km northeast of central Athens
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Marathon, Nea Makri, or the Schinias area for a short race-morning transfer; Athens works only if you plan traffic and parking carefully.
logistics.transport: A rental car or confirmed event transfer is the practical option with a bike.
logistics.food: Marathon and the surrounding coast have restaurants and groceries; bring tested race nutrition for the repeated laps.

history.founder: Bicycle Friendly Greece and the MBike team
history.origin_story: Created as Greece's first UCI Gravel World Series event by a team with cycling-media and festival experience.
history.reputation: An inaugural event with an unusually transparent course package but no results history yet.

guide_variables.race_terrain: Three 31 km loops of rural dirt, Lake Marathon dirt, two stream crossings and short steep climbs
guide_variables.race_weather: Mediterranean late autumn with meaningful rain risk

topics.lap_pacing: Dividing effort across three identical loops
topics.handling: Switching between rocky climbs, soft dirt, streams and asphalt
topics.weather: Adjusting tires and layers for November rain

marketplace_variables.race_hook: Train the third lap, not the first.
marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: Seven race-specific plans for Greece's first UCI gravel qualifier: 96 km, 1,320 metres, and the same steep ramps three times.

non_negotiables.why: The long course rides its 31 km loop three times.
The 12-percent soft-dirt climb and the stream crossings return on every lap.
The official course alternates rocky climbing, rural dirt, asphalt, soft lakeside dirt and shallow water.

final_verdict.one_liner: Greece's first UCI gravel qualifier has more verified course substance than many established races.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race it if you want UCI stakes and can respect a repeat-lap pacing plan. Wait for first-edition results if operational certainty matters more than being early.
final_verdict.alternatives: Gravel of Loutraki for an established Greek gravel event; Alentejo Gravel for a later-season European UCI qualifier.

source_review.facts_scope: The current UCI course page and race preview confirm the date, competition status, 96 km / 1,320 m long route, 65 km / 1,150 m short route, roughly 75% off-road surface, 31 km loop structure and named course features. An earlier 121 km / 2,020 m / 90% course description was superseded. Unpublished start time, fee, aid plan, cutoff and parking remain explicitly unknown.
